From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@quantara.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: production latency spikes this morning

Olga —

We saw repeated latency spikes across our batch scoring jobs between 03:40–04:10 UTC this morning. Tail latencies jumped to ~1.8s per token (typical is ~300ms) and a couple of requests timed out. This impacted the background enrichment pipeline and one public-facing endpoint briefly returned 504s.

I gathered traces attached. Can your team confirm root cause and whether this will be covered under our renewed SLA? Our account team mentioned we could look at an elevated SLA for production-critical workloads during renewal next month, but this kind of disruption puts pressure on the timeline.

Also copying procurement to flag this against the renewal calendar.

Thanks,
Liam
Head of Platform — Quantara

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@quantara.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 12:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: production latency spikes this morning

Liam, Olga —

Thanks for the traces, Liam. Early triage shows an atypical KV cache eviction pattern coinciding with an autoscaler event in the shared pool routing your workload that caused increased cold-cache decode paths. Two mitigations we’ve scoped:

- Immediate: pin a dedicated hot-slice to Quantara traffic for the next 48–72 hours to stabilize tail latency (no customer-side changes).
- Short term (2 weeks): move you to a dedicated instance pool (pilot) with baked-in KV warming and stricter autoscaler thresholds — this addresses the eviction root cause and cuts tail latencies back to normal.

We’ll push a non-disruptive config change to routing; no SDK changes required for the pin. The dedicated pilot requires an orchestrated cutover window (~30–60 minutes) with traffic warm-up; we’ll provide a runbook and will coordinate exactly so your public endpoint remains stable.

I’ll attach the KV snapshot and a short latency trace summary.

—Markus
Sr. Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: kvcache_analysis_20270210.pdf (application/pdf)]

Liam —

I can own the commercial side. Proposed approach:

- Immediate: issue a goodwill credit for the partial outage window while we confirm exact impact (I’ll request the usage logs).
- Pilot phase (30 days): dedicated instance pool at a promotional uplift of +15% over your current committed rate; SLA targeted: 99.95% availability with 200ms p95 latency target for the pinned pool.
- If pilot meets the metrics, formalize into a 12-month premium SLA addendum (pricing TBD but we’ll provide two tiers).

Next steps: I’ll create a short proposal and DocuSign packet (deal id QTR-2027-004). Can you confirm the internal approvers and any required PO timing?

—Marissa
